newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares rise on active mills trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares rise on active mills trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose on Monday as milling shares continued to dominate trade, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall index rose 0.36 points to 234.58 with a high turnover of 77.29 million pounds ($22.73 million).
A large transaction in closed firm Cairo Precise Industries accounted for about 60 million of the total volume.

"It was a usual day. There is lots of buying for Heliopolis, which rose about 20 pounds more than yesterday. When they split their shares more people came to invest, the price was more convenient," said broker Hassan Ahmed Sadeq.
The company annouced in August it would convert each of its 1,236,190 shares into four new shares to increase liquidity. The new shares had quarted the value of the original shares.
The state has also said it would sell another equity tranche to investors and Heliopolis Housing and Development jumped 27 pounds to end the day at 165 after trade worth more than 200,000 pounds.

Milling shares traded actively but ended the day only marginally higher. East Delta Flour Mills was the best of the bunch, rising 0.15 pounds to close at 35.85 after trade in more than two million pounds.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed virtually unchanged at 46.00 pounds after more than 46,000 changed hands.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills ended the day 0.70 pounds higher after trade worth about 2.4 million pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 346.55 points from Sunday's 349.60 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 166.66 points from 165.44.
